followup_explanation:
This query is a well-specified, structured writing task: draft a professional email with clear, concrete requirements (request WFH, cite the commute reason, ask for an updated offer letter with revised terms and date). The "just get it right" instruction signals the user wants precise adherence to completion criteria rather than open-ended creativity.

This maps directly onto Plover's self-reported sweet spot — reformatting and well-specified requests with clear completion criteria — which is its top-rated task family. Capability-wise, the two models are close enough on Creative Generation that there's no meaningful quality tradeoff here, and the task isn't truly open-ended generativity (which would have favored Curlew's preference profile).

Since serving cost, latency, and quality are effectively comparable, I leaned on the task-preference fit: routing the bounded, criteria-driven drafting job to the model that prefers exactly that kind of work.
